intake_analysis.case_summary: Client hired contractor for home renovation. Contractor abandoned project with 40% work incomplete after receiving $15,000 payment. Client seeking recovery of payment and additional damages for completion costs.
client_priorities: Obtain damages for additional completion costs
desired_outcomes: Compensation for additional costs to complete work
Legal precedent to prevent future contractor abuse
key_facts: Contract signed on January 15, 2024 for $25,000 total renovation
Upfront payment of $15,000 made on January 20, 2024
Work approximately 40% complete when contractor disappeared
Multiple attempts to contact contractor unsuccessful
Additional contractors estimate $10,000 to complete remaining work
intake_analysis.financial_impact: $25,000 in total damages - $15,000 paid to contractor plus $10,000 estimated completion costs
legal_claims: Breach of contract - failure to complete agreed upon work
Unjust enrichment - retention of payment without corresponding work
Potential fraud - accepting payment without intent to complete work

analyzed_documents.summary: Bank transfer receipt showing $15,000 payment to contractor
analyzed_documents.key_information: Payment made via wire transfer on January 20, 2024 to contractor's business account

analyzed_documents.summary: Text message thread between client and contractor showing work progress and eventual non-response
analyzed_documents.key_information: Messages show initial progress updates through February, then contractor stops responding to client inquiries

legal_assessment.claim_viability: Strong - clear material breach with documented evidence
legal_assessment.overall_evidence_strength: Strong - written contract, payment records, and communication logs
legal_assessment.potential_challenges: Contractor may claim work was hindered by client or cite change orders
legal_assessment.recommended_actions: File breach of contract lawsuit and pursue unjust enrichment claim
legal_assessment.demand_letter_appropriate: Yes - demand letter could prompt settlement before litigation
legal_assessment.urgency_assessment: High - statute of limitations considerations require prompt action
